subject: Is it possible to include multiple variables in each plot of a facet?

messages.author: 3b446300a01362e0
messages.subject: Is it possible to include multiple variables in each plot of a facet?
parts:
Hi there

I am struggling to generate the visualisation that I want with facet
and am not sure if what I want to do it possible. My data set is too
big to post but the code that has got me the closest to what I would
like is as follows:

ggplot(Species_data, aes(Year_vector, value)) + geom_point() +
stat_smooth(method="lm") + facet_wrap(~variable, scales = "free")

I have three different species and I have observations for each
species for each of my 6 variables. I have collapsed my data with the
melt function keeping just year (Year_vector), the observations
(value) and species(variable) as my columns. I want to plot the data
for all three species for each of the 6 variables as a function of
time (Year_vector) but I would like to have just 6 graphs in my
layout, with each one showing the data for all 3 species for each
variable (ie. 3 scatterplots per set of axes). At the moment the best
I can come up with is 18 graphs, one for each species/variable
combination.

Can anyone suggest a solution?
With thanks!

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Is it possible to include multiple variables in each plot of a facet?
parts:
Hi:

What's wrong with mapping species to color or shape as an aesthetic?

Dennis
